correctness.rationale: For n i.i.d. uniform sample points, the undirected distinct-edge nearest-neighbor graph is a chain of adjacent order statistics with an interior gap deleted exactly when it is a strict local maximum. Thus C_n=1+sum_{i=2}^{n-2} A_i, L_n=(W-sum A_i E_i)/S using independent exponential spacings with S their full n+1 sum and W internal sum. Conditioning on relative order, C is independent of W; independence from S of normalized proportions transfers Cov(C,L)=-Cov(C,B)/(n+1). Exact exponential rank probabilities give site covariance 11/27, nearest neighboring peak covariance -11/54 and distance-two covariance 139/5400; all farther disjoint triples are independent. Summing ordered covariances gives 0 for n<=3, -11/135 at n=4, -(139n+405)/(2700(n+1)) for n>=5. First moments n/3 and (7n+15)/(18(n+1)) follow directly. The source correctly distinguishes n=4 from n>=5 and undirected distinct edges from directed multiplicity. Independent rational rank-averaging on n=2..8 (seven cases) reproduced covariance, and the 5-order-statistic combinatorial count was inspected. Infinite n follows from finite-range local-dependence moment summation, not numerical extrapolation.
